Cada cifra de esta sección sale de la pl: Every figure in this section comes from the board: firmware that plays each game from a script and logs a performance line every second, or a benchmark that runs each scene five times. No emulator. At 60 fps, each frame has a 16.6 ms budget.

Cómo llega un fotograma a la pantalla: How a frame reaches the screen
Nunca hay un fotograma entero en memoria: There is never a whole frame in memory: the screen is drawn in 15 strips of 32 columns. The two cores split each strip, left half and right half, in internal RAM, while DMA sends the previous strip to the panel.
Se repite la misma escena quitando una c: The same scene, replayed with one thing removed each time. In gotico, blending the two moonbeams on the fly ate 13 ms a frame: now they come pre-painted into the background, and the game went from 31 to 60 fps.
gotico, antes del arreglo (ms por fotogr: gotico, before the fix (ms per frame)
laberinto: el raycast antes y después de: laberinto: the raycast before and after optimising it (ms per frame)
Un fotograma lógico de 240×160 con conte: A 240×160 logical frame of synthetic content, best of five runs, as a share of one core's time at 60 fps. The console has two cores.

El motor, los ejemplos, las herramientas: The engine, examples, tools and this site were written in conversation with Claude Code: every idea was tried in the simulator, measured on the board and corrected based on what the board showed.
The art, generated and made to fit.
Los aspectos que lo necesitan (Neo Geo,: The looks that call for it (Neo Geo, CPS2, 32-bit) use AI-generated images. The engine's tools cut them out, scale them to the right height, split them into frames and reduce them to the console's palette. The low-res looks are drawn with code.
Cada ejemplo tiene un guion que lo juega: Every example has a script that plays it automatically. On the computer, it checks each frame's checksum against the stored one; on the board, it logs the fps every second. Optimisations don't change a single pixel.

A clean clone of the repository, one request at a time and no questions answered: Codex read AGENTS.md, built the engine, followed the recipe for the look and wrote a script that plays its game, iterating until it passed. Each game was then measured on the console, running that script. Codex 0.155 with gpt-6-sol, medium reasoning. (The requests were written in Spanish and are translated here.)
Tres encargos: el juego (4 min 41 s); el: Three requests: the game (4 min 41 s), its AI-generated art (10 min 8 s; it then ran at 30 fps), and getting it to 60 fps on the console with its own ground layer (3 min 45 s). No touch-ups by hand.
Un goblin original para un beat 'em up d: An original goblin enemy for a fantasy beat-em-up: small, wiry and hunched, green skin, huge pointed ears, a ragged brown loincloth, a rusty curved dagger. Full body, facing left. Style: a mid-1990s arcade sprite, crisp hard pixel edges, a bold dark outline, about 15 colours. Transparent background.
Las herramientas del motor quitan el fon: The engine's tools remove the background, split the frames, bring them to the same scale with their feet on the same line, and reduce them to 15 colours. Then each one is checked by eye.
Cada punto es un segundo de partida en l: Each point is one second of play on the board, from the performance line logged every second while a script plays the game. Dashed: the first measurement; solid: today's. The first second loads the scene and doesn't count in the figures.

¿Quieres subir una versión nueva de un j: Want to send a new version of a game that is already in the Library? Send the form again, from the same GitHub account and with the same ID (the id in your game.json): once approved, it replaces the old one, and anyone already playing keeps their saved games. The game's page can take a little while to show the changes.
Una consola virtual como la Game Boy Adv: A virtual console like the Game Boy Advance: 240×160 with four layers, 128 sprites, palettes, transparency and per-line effects, and on top, text and panels at 480×320. Also PlayStation-style textured 3D faces, lights, particles and cut-out animation.
Mode 7, primera persona a lo Wolfenstein: Mode 7, first person in the style of Wolfenstein 3D, voxel landscapes, grids with field of view and pathfinding, generated dungeons, swarms of hundreds of bullets and levels drawn in Tiled or LDtk.
Efectos hechos con recetas o con números: Sound effects made from recipes or from numbers, four synth voices like the Game Boy Advance's, instruments, PlayStation reverbs, layered music that changes on the bar line, and .mod, .xm and .s3m modules.
Pantalla táctil con lápiz y varios dedos: Touch screen with a stylus and several fingers, microphone, the LED and the battery, video from the card and games between nearby consoles, no router. The menu opens over any game, with settings, favourites and achievements.
Lua, con más de treinta librerías dentro: Lua, with more than thirty libraries built in: physics, particles, stories, camera, scenes, artificial intelligence, generated levels, Celeste's movement and the adventure kit. Games save without freezing, a script tests every game by itself and a profiler says where the time goes.

Comentarios y votos en cada juego, y el: Comments and votes on every game, and PlayStation-style 3D measured on the board: lights, warps, perspective and clipping.
Caras 3D con textura y cámaras, animació: Textured 3D faces and cameras, cut-out animation, glowing particles and a transitions library.
Instrumentos, envíos y eco para el sonid: Instruments, sends and echo for sound, Game Boy Advance-faithful blending and a pinball with real physics.
Lápiz y varios dedos en la pantalla táct: Stylus and several fingers on the touch screen, two screens in the simulator, the POWERED BY PINYOL splash in every game, Lua at twice the speed, eleven new examples and firmware 0.3.0.
de un núcleo para el sonido de un juego: of one core for the sound of a simple game; with layered music, up to 18%
El menú de la consola sobre cualquier ju: The console's menu over any game, with settings, favourites and achievements; games between consoles over the radio; Celeste-style movement; and code running from PSRAM, which speeds up the world by up to 30%.
Módulos XM y S3M, canciones de FamiStudi: XM and S3M modules, FamiStudio songs, rollback between consoles, field of view on grids, the console's memory reorganised and firmware 0.4.0.
mesh(): modelos 3D dibujados en C, y cua: mesh(): 3D models drawn in C, and four games with the 32-bit look: Selva, Niebla, Recortes and Cajas. Firmware 0.5.0.
Un corredor al estilo de los 32 bits: la: A 32-bit style runner: the camera follows a fox that jumps crates, picks up fruit and dodges pits along a path between trees. Everything is low-polygon textured faces, flat light, fog and wobbling vertices, drawn with mesh(). And a menu that shows every trick.
Una calle de noche, una linterna y algo: A street at night, a flashlight and something following you. Fixed cameras that change as you cross the street, tank controls, fog that hides the distance and a radio that crackles when it gets close. All with mesh(), like the 32-bit horror games. And a menu that shows the tricks.
Un juego de ritmo de llamada y respuesta: A call-and-response rhythm game with cut-out paper characters, like the 32-bit ones: the toad master sings a phrase with the buttons and you repeat it in time. The dolls are quads that fold like paper, the sets run on the PPU's layers and the music plays live on the synthesizer's voices. And a menu that shows the tricks.
Un juego de lucha uno contra uno con luc: A one-on-one fighting game with blocky fighters, like the first 32-bit ones: side camera, punch, kick, sweep, block and jump, best of three rounds against the machine. Each fighter is eleven textured boxes moved with kinematics in Lua and drawn with mesh(). And a menu that shows the tricks.
Una aventura de acción como las de la úl: An action adventure like the Game Boy's last era: an island, a village, a cave under the mountain and a cherry tree that has not bloomed. Four tones, 8x8 tiles, 16x16 sprites and a menu that shows how the console did it.
Una mina a la manera de un juego de ZX S: A mine the way a ZX Spectrum game drew one, from the tape loading: eight one-screen rooms, two-colour blocks with their colour clash, flashing keys, belts, crumbling floors and a beeper as the only voice. And a menu that shows how the machine did it.
Un puzle de deslizamiento por tumbas com: A PICO-8-style tomb sliding puzzle: the explorer slides until he hits something, collects gems, dodges spikes and looks for the exit. Sixteen 128x128 levels with quicksand, cracking walls, portals, keys and one-way gates, each with its par in moves. And a menu that shows what a cartridge is made of: the sixteen-colour palette, the map, the four channels and the fades.
Una maquinita LCD de bolsillo como las G: A pocket LCD game like a Game & Watch: a juggler throws balls from hand to hand, every figure is a fixed shape that lights or goes dark over a printed picture, the world moves a step at a time with beeps, and when nobody plays it is a clock. Two games, A and B, and a menu that shows how a segment screen works.
Un correr y disparar: cocineros contra g: A run and gun: cooks against mechanical seagulls, with a tractor and a boss.
Un plataformas de Game Boy Advance con u: A Game Boy Advance platformer with a pirate, a parallax jungle and jewels
Un plataformas de botín en cuatro mundos: A loot platformer in four worlds, with parallax, rippling water and a boss.
Un run and gun de Neo Geo: un cocinero e: A Neo Geo run and gun: a cook on a tractor in a village street, shooting at mechanical seagulls
Un correr y disparar a la manera de la N: A run and gun the Neo Geo way: six cooks against an invasion of mechanical seagulls in a coastal village, with a tractor and a giant boss. Everything at 480x320, with characters painted frame by frame, and a menu that shows the machine's tricks.
Un plataformas de botín y tesoros como l: A loot-and-treasure platformer like the Game Boy Advance's: four worlds, four jewel pieces a level, a frog switch that starts the escape, and a boss. Line parallax, 16-colour palettes, rotating sprites and the line effects their games used, with what they cost on the console explained in the menu.
